meta.title: PepsiCo and the Price of Volume
meta.dek: PepsiCo cut prices to win back North American snackers, and it worked on volume. The profit did not come with it. What does the stock price assume about whether it ever will?
meta.type: Consumer staples — global convenient foods + beverages

verdict.sentence: Both Oct 8 kill criteria failed: full-year guidance was cut, and North American snacks revenue slipped even as share rose. The pre-committed move to Watch applies; the probability-weighted case returns [[pw_return]] against the 13% hurdle.
verdict.breaks_if: the price investment in North American snacks never earns back margin: PepsiCo Foods North America revenue flat to down while volume share rises, with core margin still falling through 2027.

call: The Oct 8 print failed both tests written the day before: core constant-currency EPS guidance fell to +1–2% from the low end of +4–6%, and PFNA net revenue slipped 0.3% even though volume share rose. Each failure was pre-committed to Watch, and the rebuilt case agrees: the probability-weighted value of [[pw_ev]] returns [[pw_return]] a year, below the hurdle. The market had already priced worse; the stock rose 3.7% on the day. At $128 an ordinary 8% return needs only about [[Priced-in.cagr]] EPS growth, and in scenario terms a [[implied_bear]] Bear probability against our [[Bear.prob]]. That gap is not yet an opportunity, because the evidence moved the wrong way: the price cuts are buying volume but not revenue, PFNA core profit fell 12%, and Q3's 3% core profit growth needed 4 points of tariff refunds. The case clears 13% only at [[entry]]. The number that settles it is the FY2027 guide in February.

tests.claim: That the new cost programme is real money.
tests.test: by the Q4 release (early February 2027), PepsiCo quantifies the structural cost programme and the Elliott-committed North America supply-chain review, either as ≥$1B of savings or as a reaffirmed ≥100 bps 2026–28 core margin target.
tests.if_fail: move 7 points from Bull to Base (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test1.verb]]** (entry [[test1.entry]]).

tests.claim: That 2026 is the trough year for earnings growth.
tests.test: FY2027 guidance in the Q4 release (February 2027) calls for at least +4% core constant-currency EPS.
tests.if_fail: Base EPS growth falls to 3% a year (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test2.verb]]** (entry [[test2.entry]]).

tests.test: in the FY2026 10-K (February 2027), core operating margin is up year over year, capex is under 5% of sales, and owner earnings cover the dividend. This test is tracking to fail: core margin is −25 bps year to date and the Q4 North America margin is guided down.
tests.if_fail: move 7 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]** (entry [[test3.entry]]); the stage stays mature ex-growth.

return_math.epv: $65–75 per share (five-year owner earnings of $8.1B ÷ 8%; enterprise basis at the 14.2% median margin ≈$65); about 42% of the price pays for growth. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits above EPV because it keeps inflation-level growth after year five; a no-growth Bear would be ≈$75.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull needs ~4% nominal (~1.5% real) sales growth, the median for companies above $50B of sales: plausible. The Base reconciles to ~3% organic growth and a flat margin: probable. The Bear is now as probable as the Base, because 2026 is its first year of evidence.
return_math.year_ten: Mature ex-growth: the value is a 3–4% grower's multiple plus the yield. Nothing in the growth levers changes that, so the terminal multiple does the work.
